note: Opportunities Sheila (9) can take part in now, with an adult where the source says so, from organizations the owner has pointed at. Every item names its source URL and the date it was checked; confirm details on the page before signing up. Never add a fact without a source.

forms.name: Community Service Hours Log
forms.note: Seattle Humane's official monthly log: one row per session with date, time in, description of activity, time out, total time, and a signature. The Reports page prints this format filled in from the tracker; take it along for the signature.

contact.address: Seattle Children's In-Kind Donations, M/S RC.3.800, 4800 Sand Point Way NE, Seattle, WA 98105

items.title: No-sew cat blankets
items.summary: Make small fleece blankets for the cats waiting to be adopted.
details: All the cats in Seattle Humane's care receive a blanket or towel to make their cubby more comfortable; most of the time a cat's special blanket goes home with them when they are adopted.
Blankets around 18 × 20 inches are suggested for cats.
Written and video instructions for making no-sew blankets are on the project page.
Community service hours are recorded on Seattle Humane's monthly Community Service Hours Log, one row per session with time in, time out and a signature (form linked on the organization).

ages.note: No age limit stated on the page.

items.commitment: One sitting per batch; drop off when you have a few.
items.location: At home; deliver to Seattle Humane
items.howTo: Follow the no-sew instructions on the project page, then bring the blankets to the shelter. Contact Education Services for drop-off details.

items.title: Homemade cat toys from recycled objects
items.summary: Turn old socks and paper tubes into catnip toys for shelter cats.
details: Old socks become catnip toys when stuffed with scrap paper, toilet paper tubes, or other crinkly items with catnip.
The project page lists more ways to make cat toys from recycled or reusable objects.
Community service hours are recorded on Seattle Humane's monthly Community Service Hours Log, one row per session with time in, time out and a signature (form linked on the organization).

ages.note: No age limit stated on the page.

items.location: At home; deliver to Seattle Humane
items.howTo: Make the toys following the project page, then bring them to the shelter with any blankets.

items.title: Pet food drive
items.summary: Organize a pet food drive in the neighborhood or at school.
details: Donations of pet food, supplies and toys are always appreciated.
Items are distributed through Oogie's Ohana Pet Food Bank at Seattle Humane, which helps provide 1 million meals each year to pets in the community.
Youth can help pets and earn school service hours by donating, fundraising or supporting the pet food bank.
Community service hours are recorded on Seattle Humane's monthly Community Service Hours Log, one row per session with time in, time out and a signature (form linked on the organization).

ages.note: No age limit stated; collecting from neighbors and delivering needs an adult.

items.commitment: A few weeks of collecting, then one delivery.
items.location: Neighborhood or school; deliver to Seattle Humane
items.howTo: Pick a collection window, tell neighbors or the class what to bring, then deliver the donations to the shelter. Email Education Services for current needs.

items.title: Wish-list donation drive for patients and families
items.summary: Collect new toys, books, blankets or toiletries from the hospital's wish list.
details: Youth can hold a donation drive to collect toys, books, blankets, toiletries or other high-need items for patients and families; groups can collect and donate items from the hospital's wish list.
Only new toys can be accepted, to reduce the spread of infection.
Blankets are a particular need: the goal is that each child admitted overnight receives one, and they are often kept for years as a keepsake.
Items bought online and shipped straight from the retailer to the hospital are preferred, because they do not have to be quarantined. New items can also be mailed to the In-Kind Donations address.
Drop-offs at the hospital are accepted by scheduling in advance.

ages.note: No age limit stated for running a drive; delivering needs an adult.

items.commitment: A few weeks of collecting, then one scheduled delivery or a shipment.
items.location: Neighborhood or school; ship or deliver to Seattle Children's
items.howTo: Download the wish list (seattlechildrens.org/globalassets/documents/giving/wish-list.pdf), collect only new items, then email the In-Kind Gift Coordinator to schedule the drop-off or ship items directly.

items.title: Make blankets or comfort items (approval first)
items.summary: Handmade items for patients are accepted case by case; ask before making a batch.
details: Handmade items are accepted on a case-by-case basis with advance approval from the In-Kind Gift Coordinator.
Blankets bring much comfort and are a particular need; each child admitted overnight should receive one.
Groups can help by holding a toy drive or making items to donate.

ages.note: No age limit stated; approval and delivery go through an adult.

items.commitment: One batch at a time, after approval.
items.howTo: Email inkind@seattlechildrens.org (or call 206-987-7078) describing what you want to make, wait for approval, then make the batch and schedule the drop-off.

items.title: Hospital grounds projects (groups of 3–10)
items.summary: Small groups help the grounds staff outdoors; the playroom is adults only.
details: Groups of 3–10 people can assist with grounds projects.
Playroom sessions are for small groups under five people, ages 18 and older; volunteer positions at the hospital start at 16, and patient-facing roles at 18.

ages.note: Group opportunity arranged with the volunteer office; hospital volunteer roles themselves start at 16 (18 for patient-facing).

items.howTo: Gather a group of 3–10 (a family counts) and ask the volunteer office (206-987-7078) whether a grounds project is open to children with adults.

items.title: Host a fundraiser or form a junior guild
items.summary: Turn an activity you love into a way to support the hospital.
details: Hosting an event or promotion is a creative way for volunteers to help patients and families at Seattle Children's.
Youth can form a junior guild to turn activities they love into ways to support Seattle Children's.
The hospital publishes a getting-involved guide for middle and high school students.

ages.note: The published guide is for middle and high school students; younger children can run a small fundraiser with an adult.

items.commitment: One event, or an ongoing guild.
items.howTo: Read the middle & high school guide (seattlechildrens.org/globalassets/documents/giving/guilds/resources/getting-involved---a-guide-for-middle-and-high-school-students---seattle-childrens.pdf), pick an activity, and register the fundraiser through Community Fundraising (seattlechildrens.org/giving/community-fundraising/).
